title: Introduction to tidyEmoji
text: Emoji everywhere modern text — social-media posts, product reviews, chat support logs, survey free-text — carry information plain words . Yet summarising emoji corpus surprisingly awkward. Unicode interact cleanly regular expressions, every code point emoji, single visible emoji often built several code points joined together. Counting “many posts contain emoji” “emoji common” hand quickly becomes painful. tidyEmoji removes friction. provides small family verbs take data frame name text column, return tidy data frames drop straight dplyr/ggplot2 workflow: Two design choices worth highlighting: Grapheme-aware detection. Detection performed whole grapheme clusters, skin-tone modifiers (👍🏽) zero-width-joiner sequences family emoji (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦) treated single emoji rather split component parts. illustrated extraction section. Tidy default. Every verb returns tibble, follows verb(data, text_column) convention, supports unquoted column names, functions compose naturally pipe. Grouping composes : verbs work row time carry group_by() result, dplyr::mutate() dplyr::filter() , ones pool across rows – counts, co-occurrence tables, time series – warn ignore return one corpus-wide answer. See ?tidyEmoji full contract.
code: library(tidyEmoji) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2)

text: Throughout vignette use sample text collected Atlanta, Georgia. data happens come social-media corpus, nothing specific platform — data frame text column . actual text lives full_text column, column pass tidyEmoji verb.

title: Introduction to tidyEmoji
text: emoji_summary() answers first question one usually asks new corpus: much emoji ? returns one-row tibble number entries contain least one emoji total number entries. entry counted regardless many emoji holds. , 560 2,000 entries (28%) contain least one emoji.
code: summary_tbl <- ata_tweets %>%   emoji_summary(full_text)  summary_tbl #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   n_with_emoji n_total #>          <int>   <int> #> 1          560    2000

title: Introduction to tidyEmoji
text: emoji_filter() keeps rows whose text contains least one emoji, preserving every original column. useful want compare emoji-bearing emoji-free text, restrict analysis emoji subset. (emoji_tweets() synonym retained backward compatibility.)
code: ata_tweets %>%   emoji_filter(full_text) #> # A tibble: 560 × 1 #>    full_text                                                                     #>    <chr>                                                                         #>  1 Whole Family gone and I’m stuck here in Brunswick 😭                          #>  2 This time last year I was blasting fever nonstop by Wizkid 😭                 #>  3 Phone dry asf 🙄                                                              #>  4 When I gave my life to Christ, I was able to see people as imperfect, but st… #>  5 Everyone needs self care days❤️                                                #>  6 R u sears rn 🤦🏽‍♀️                                                               #>  7 Gucci wit some dope runnas head huncho top gunna u a sto runna😭              #>  8 i’m thinking insomnia cause they got this caramel apple pie cookie. 😋        #>  9 i deadass listen to the music everyday lmao🥲                                 #> 10 Im ona block where ya barley can be at  if you try get shot down 😈           #> # ℹ 550 more rows

title: Introduction to tidyEmoji
text: tidyEmoji offers three complementary ways pull emoji text, depending shape output want.

title: Introduction to tidyEmoji
text: emoji_extract_nest() leaves data unchanged except added list-column, .emoji_unicode, holding emoji found row. original data structure preserved, makes convenient intermediate step.
code: ata_tweets %>%   emoji_extract_nest(full_text) %>%   select(full_text, .emoji_unicode) #> # A tibble: 2,000 × 2 #>    full_text                                                      .emoji_unicode #>    <chr>                                                          <list>         #>  1 "Was Justin Bieber ever at any BLM March/protest this past su… <chr [0]>      #>  2 "Whole Family gone and I’m stuck here in Brunswick 😭"         <chr [1]>      #>  3 "38 years old and I still get distracted while cleaning my ro… <chr [0]>      #>  4 "This time last year I was blasting fever nonstop by Wizkid 😭… <chr [1]>      #>  5 "Kanye is a just a black man with a lot of confidence and y’a… <chr [0]>      #>  6 "Feel like being my inner self today"                          <chr [0]>      #>  7 "Peep toe boots irk my sole."                                  <chr [0]>      #>  8 "Nah the biggest naruto fans be trying call one piece long li… <chr [0]>      #>  9 "if my shoes don’t arrive by next Friday imma be pissed"       <chr [0]>      #> 10 "Phone dry asf 🙄"                                             <chr [1]>      #> # ℹ 1,990 more rows

title: Introduction to tidyEmoji
text: emoji_extract_unnest() returns long, tidy table one row per (entry, emoji) pair: .row_number records position entry data, .emoji_unicode emoji, .emoji_count many times emoji occurs entry. Entries without emoji dropped. can use plot many emoji emoji-bearing entry contains:  overwhelming majority emoji-bearing entries carry just one emoji, long, thin tail emoji-heavy entries.
code: emoji_per_tweet <- ata_tweets %>%   emoji_extract_unnest(full_text)  emoji_per_tweet #> # A tibble: 696 × 3 #>    .row_number .emoji_unicode .emoji_count #>          <int> <chr>                 <int> #>  1           2 😭                        1 #>  2           4 😭                        1 #>  3          10 🙄                        1 #>  4          15 😂                        1 #>  5          17 ❤️                         1 #>  6          30 🤦🏽‍♀️                        1 #>  7          31 😭                        1 #>  8          33 😋                        1 #>  9          42 🥲                        1 #> 10          45 😈                        1 #> # ℹ 686 more rows emoji_per_tweet %>%   group_by(.row_number) %>%   summarise(n_emoji = sum(.emoji_count)) %>%   ggplot(aes(n_emoji)) +   geom_bar() +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 15)) +   labs(x = "Number of emoji in the entry",        y = "Number of entries",        title = "Most emoji-bearing entries contain a single emoji")

title: Introduction to tidyEmoji
text: Modern emoji frequently composed several code points: base emoji plus skin-tone modifier, several emoji joined zero-width joiners. tidyEmoji detects emoji level grapheme clusters, stay intact. example contains exactly two emoji — one family one thumbs-— tidyEmoji counts rather splitting family four people separating thumb skin tone:
code: demo <- data.frame(   text = c("our family \U0001F468‍\U0001F469‍\U0001F467‍\U0001F466",            "great work \U0001F44D\U0001F3FD") )  demo %>%   emoji_extract_unnest(text) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   .row_number .emoji_unicode .emoji_count #>         <int> <chr>                 <int> #> 1           1 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦                        1 #> 2           2 👍🏽                        1

title: Introduction to tidyEmoji
text: Emoji now preprocessing decision every LLM pipeline, decision matters: inflate token counts several-fold, models disambiguate poorly. emoji_token_cost() gives exact sizes plus clearly-labelled estimate – pass real tokeniser tokenizer number matters: emoji_sanitize() applies one named policy column. capability new – exists across emoji_to_text() extraction verbs – named argument shows script diff methods section, point:
code: ata_tweets %>%   emoji_token_cost(full_text) %>%   filter(.emoji_n > 0) %>%   summarise(emoji = sum(.emoji_n),             bytes = sum(.emoji_bytes),             codepoints = sum(.emoji_codepoints),             est_tokens = sum(.emoji_token_estimate)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   emoji bytes codepoints est_tokens #>   <int> <int>      <int>      <int> #> 1   900  4437       1166       2245 demo_llm <- data.frame(text = "ship it \U0001f680 today") for (p in c("keep", "strip", "name", "shortcode", "placeholder")) {   cat(format(p, width = 12), emoji_sanitize(demo_llm, text, policy = p)$text,       "\n") } #> keep         ship it 🚀 today  #> strip        ship it today  #> name         ship it rocket today  #> shortcode    ship it :rocket: today  #> placeholder  ship it [emoji] today

title: Introduction to tidyEmoji

title: tidyEmoji — Roadmap for 0.5.0

Participants preferred PREVIEW, leaves judgement human. Practitioner guidance converges two rules: avoid runs emoji, prefer sentence-final placement emoji sandwiched words. finding round, tidyEmoji already every primitive needs: emoji_to_text(format = "name") PREVIEW, emoji_position() + emoji_ngrams() + emoji_ratio() ALERT. See §4.3. Reinforces modifier theme. Digital Skin, Digital Bias: Uncovering Tone-Based Biases LLMs Emoji Embeddings (ACM Web Conference 2026, doi:10.1145/3774904.3792508) — first large-scale comparative study skin-tone bias across emoji embedding models (emoji2vec, emoji-sw2v) four modern LLMs. Skin tone cosmetic attribute glyph; propagates downstream representations. Digital Colourism? Understanding Emoji Skin Tone Preferences Among Indian-Origin Users (BCS HCI 2025) — tone preference culturally patterned well beyond US/UK samples earlier work used. 2025 work reports women likely men use tones matching value range options — group difference, exactly emoji_tone_summary(group_by =) make one-liner. Reinforces LLM theme (0.4.0 shipped plumbing; case got stronger). EMODIS now published AAAI 2026 (arXiv 2511.07193) number worth quoting: human annotators 88.5% versus GPT-4 58.8% context-dependent emoji disambiguation — roughly 30-point gap. Small Symbols, Big Risks: Emoticon Semantic Confusion LLMs (arXiv 2601.07885, 2026) — six LLMs, average confusion ratio 38%, 90% confused responses “silent failures”: syntactically valid output deviates intent. strongest argument yet emoji_sanitize() explicit, recorded decision. Emoji-Based Jailbreaking Large Language Models — supports defensive framing future emoji_obfuscation_scan(), discipline reporting structural anomalies rather shipping attack patterns. Applied domains — new syntheses, new API pressure. Emojis Marketing Advertising: Systematic Literature Review (Behavioral Sciences 2025, doi:10.3390/bs15111490), T-C-C-M framework; field “growing volume yet immature”. Emoji-based marketing consumer behavior: systematic literature review (Cogent Business & Management 2026, doi:10.1080/23311975.2026.2669001), 45 articles, ADO framework. Health-communication reviews cover food safety, behaviour guidance doctor-patient communication. None asks new verb: emoji_type() / emoji_faceness() emoji_congruence() already carry variables literatures use. Continue ship clinical instrument. Semantics embeddings — still urgent. pleading face (Emoji 11.0) is detected but absent from the 2015 lexicon   d <- tibble::tibble(text = c("no emoji", "hi \U0001F600", "new \U0001F97A", NA_character_))   r <- emoji_sentiment(d, text)   expect_identical(r$.emoji_n,        c(0L, 1L, 1L, 0L))   expect_identical(r$.emoji_n_scored, c(NA_integer_, 1L, 0L, NA_integer_))   expect_true(is.na(r$.emoji_sentiment[3])) })  test_that("new columns on user data are dotted (roadmap S1.6)", {   d <- tibble::tibble(id = 1:3, text = c("hi \U0001F600", "none", NA_character_))   for (f in list(emoji_sentiment, emoji_position, emoji_ratio,                  emoji_density, emoji_type, emoji_faceness)) {     added <- setdiff(names(f(d, text)), names(d))     expect_true(all(grepl("^\\.emoji", added)))   } })  test_that("emoji_score() agrees with the specific scorer (roadmap S1.8)", {   d <- tibble::tibble(text = c("hi \U0001F600", "none"))   expect_equal(emoji_sentiment(d, text)$.emoji_sentiment,                emoji_score(d, text, lexicon = "sentiment")$.emoji_score) })  test_that("emoji_sanitize() policies form the documented loss ladder (S1.9)", {   orig <- "great \U0001F600 work \U0001F44D today"   d <- tibble::tibble(text = orig)   restore <- function(pol) {     out <- emoji_sanitize(d, text, policy = pol)$text     text_to_emoji(tibble::tibble(text = out), text)$text   }   expect_identical(restore("keep"), orig)        # strip must not leave doubled whitespace   expect_false(grepl("  ", emoji_sanitize(d, text, policy = "strip")$text)) })  test_that("emoji_context() windows handle both boundaries (roadmap S1.9)", {   d <- tibble::tibble(text = c("\U0001F600 starts here now", "ends here now \U0001F600"))   r <- emoji_context(d, text, window = 2, unit = "word")   expect_identical(r$.emoji_context_left[1],  "")   expect_identical(r$.emoji_context_right[2], "") })  test_that("detection handles keycaps and valid tone sequences as single units (S1.2)", {   one_unit <- c("1\uFE0F\u20E3", "#\uFE0F\u20E3", "\u2764\uFE0F",                 "\U0001F1FA\U0001F1F8", "\U0001F44B\U0001F3FB")   for (g in one_unit) {     expect_equal(emoji_summary(tibble::tibble(text = g), text)$n_with_emoji, 1L)   } })  test_that("emoji are invariant under Unicode normalisation (roadmap S1.4)", {   skip_if_not_installed("stringi")   glyphs <- c("\U0001F44B\U0001F3FB", "\u2764\uFE0F",               "\U0001F1FA\U0001F1F8", "1\uFE0F\u20E3")   for (g in glyphs) {     expect_identical(stringi::stri_trans_nfc(g), g)     expect_identical(stringi::stri_trans_nfd(g), g)   } })  test_that("zero-row and all-NA input are handled, not errored (roadmap S1.5)", {   z  <- tibble::tibble(text = character(0))   na <- tibble::tibble(text = rep(NA_character_, 3))   for (f in list(emoji_sentiment, emoji_position, emoji_frequency,                  emoji_ratio, emoji_type, emoji_tokens)) {     expect_no_error(f(z, text))     expect_no_error(f(na, text))   } })

text: 969 rows, covering 19% distinct emoji tidyEmoji can detect (3790 distinct codepoint keys reference table emoji 16.0.0; see emoji_provenance() version ). Two caveats figure, consequences lexicon built 2015 tweets: 233 969 rows reference table – see Detection limitations – nothing added Unicode 2015 . emoji_sentiment()'s .emoji_n_scored reports shortfall per row.

title: Emoji Sentiment Ranking lexicon — emoji_sentiment_lexicon
text: Many glyphs lexicon stored unqualified, text-presentation form: single code point U+FE0F emoji-presentation variation selector. best-known bare heart, U+2764; others include white smiling face (U+263A), heavy check mark (U+2714) black rightwards arrow (U+27A1). lexicon also contains characters emoji (box-drawing characters, copyright registered signs, replacement character), inherited tweets built . grapheme-aware detection used throughout package treat text-presentation code points emoji, row whose "emoji" one counted scored – behaves contained emoji. affects detection , never join: supply qualified form (red heart U+2764 U+FE0F, say) resolves lexicon entry, every lookup goes codepoint key ignores U+FE0F.

title: tidyEmoji 0.3.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-08-04

title: tidyEmoji 0.3.0
text: emoji_emotion() scores row’s emoji across eight Plutchik emotions (anger, anticipation, disgust, fear, joy, sadness, surprise, trust), using new bundled emoji_emotion_lexicon (EmoTag1200, Shoeb & de Melo 2020, MIT). Supports long form (long = TRUE) one row per (row, emotion). emoji_emotion_label() adds dominant emotion per row. pluggable lexicon API: emoji_lexicons() lists bundled registered lexicons, register_emoji_lexicon() adds , emoji_score() generic scorer verbs share. emoji_sentiment() gains lexicon argument (default "novak2015", unchanged behaviour). Relational analysis. emoji_pairs() returns tidy, graph-ready edge list (item1, item2, n) emoji co-occur document — row document, supply doc_id pool rows — directed = TRUE order pairs first appearance. emoji_cooccurrence() optional diagonal (emoji’s document frequency). emoji_ngrams() slides window row’s emoji reading order returns one row per consecutive n-gram. Structural metrics. emoji_position() reports emoji sit text (first/last character position mean relative position [0, 1]), emoji_density() reports emoji per character per token, emoji_ratio() reports share text’s characters emoji plus .emoji_only flag. emoji_dfm() builds document--emoji feature table (weightings: counts, binary, tf-idf), keeping every document — including emoji-free ones — result binds row--row outcome columns modelling workflows. corpus-level verbs (emoji_pairs(), emoji_cooccurrence(), emoji_ngrams(), emoji_dfm()) canonicalise glyphs package’s codepoint key, qualified unqualified forms emoji (example victory hand without U+FE0F) count one node/feature. emoji_frequency() intentionally still reports exact extracted glyph. emoji_to_text() replaces emoji text column Unicode names shortcodes (demojize — useful accessibility NLP preprocessing), text_to_emoji() inverse (emojize). Vector helpers as_emoji_name(), as_emoji_shortcode() as_emoji() ad-hoc conversion. emoji_search() finds emoji keyword, name shortcode returns tidy tibble matches. New bundled dataset emoji_emotion_lexicon. tidyEmoji hex logo! appears README pkgdown site (man/figures/logo.svg vector master, logo.png raster copy).

title: tidyEmoji 0.3.0
text: Grapheme-aware detection now covers newer zero-width-joiner sequences. upstream emoji regex knows ZWJ sequences current built, reported later ones — face exhaling, face spiral eyes, heart fire, people holding hands, skin-toned handshakes, “woman: blond hair”, around 630 others — component emoji. tidyEmoji now re-joins (ZWJ two emoji always binds one grapheme cluster). Previously emoji inflated counts, resolved wrong name, split several co-occurrence nodes stopped emoji_ratio() recognising emoji-row; fixed. Emoji separated anything ZWJ unaffected. Extraction location now sliced spans, verb can disagree another emoji starts ends. text_to_emoji() longer misses :shortcode: follows unrelated colon. "meet 10:30 :grinning:" "https://example.org :grinning:" previously came back unchanged, permissive :...: pattern consumed shortcode’s opening colon; shortcode tokens now matched character set GitHub-style aliases actually use. emoji_pairs() emoji_dfm() order glyphs C locale, glyph lands item1 order dfm’s tied columns longer depend session’s collation. Results now reproducible across machines. emoji_lexicons() longer reports glyph column score dimension lexicon registered "emoji". emoji_emotion(long = TRUE) longer drops user column named .row_number. emoji_ngrams(n = Inf) gives documented error instead coercion warning followed “missing value TRUE/FALSE needed”. emoji_to_text() several times faster: locates emoji whole column rather per row. emoji_density() returns .emoji_per_token = 0 (NA) whitespace-text, matching .emoji_per_char documented “emoji -> 0” contract (#1). as_emoji() accepts spaced Unicode names produced as_emoji_name() (routing reference table), as_emoji(as_emoji_name(x)) round-trips instead returning NA (#2). ?emoji_sentiment_lexicon now explains lexicon entries stored unqualified, text-presentation code points (bare heart U+2764 without U+FE0F, white smiling face, heavy check mark, …) therefore detected text, notes qualified form resolves entry (#3). help pages longer embed raw emoji glyphs, reference manual builds PDF; ?register_emoji_lexicon longer points internal development file. emoji_search() matches literally, queries containing regex metacharacters (example +1 alias) safe error. emoji_to_text(format = "shortcode") now always emits emoji’s canonical (first) GitHub-style alias — one reported emoji_frequency() as_emoji_shortcode() — wrap template honoured. Emoji known name/shortcode left place rather dropped text. emoji_to_text() text_to_emoji() keep NA text entries NA. emoji_emotion() emoji_emotion_label() accept registered data-frame emotion lexicons (subset eight Plutchik dimensions), just bundled "emotag1200". Registered lexicons resolve stored normalised key, register_emoji_lexicon(= ) works glyph column name emoji_sentiment() emoji_emotion(). emoji_frequency() (therefore top_n_emojis()) breaks count ties glyph, making output order deterministic. emoji_lexicons() longer lists custom lexicon’s glyph/key columns among score dimensions. package help page (?tidyEmoji) documents output naming contract shared verbs. rlang moved Suggests Imports (tidy-eval capture new optional doc_id argument); already hard transitive dependency, installed footprint unchanged. Grouped data frames passed emoji_pairs(), emoji_cooccurrence() emoji_dfm() warn grouping ignored — use doc_id express per-group structure. vignette header longer carries build date. DESCRIPTION Title Description broadened cover emotions, translation, search, co-occurrence, structural metrics feature tables; version bumped 0.3.0.

title: tidyEmoji 0.2.1
text: Emoji name, shortcode category now resolve codepoint-normalised key sentiment, emoji carrying U+FE0F variation selector longer get NA metadata, longer dropped emoji_categorize(), longer disappear top_n_emojis(duplicated = TRUE). whole package now agrees “contains emoji” means: emoji_summary() emoji_filter() use detection extraction verbs. emoji_sentiment() gains .emoji_n_scored (emoji actually found lexicon), distinct .emoji_n. top_n_emojis(n =) counts distinct emoji rather rows, breaks ties deterministically, keeps emoji GitHub-style alias, preserves exact extracted glyph duplicated mode (one row per distinct alias; left_join instead inner_join). emoji_extract_unnest() now uses .row_number (dotted) avoid collision user columns dplyr::row_number. emoji_summary() column names renamed emoji_tweets/total_tweets n_with_emoji/n_total. old names longer available release. emoji_tweets() soft-deprecated favour emoji_filter(). Faster large corpora: codepoint keys computed unique glyph set rather per row emoji_sentiment() emoji_categorize(). Grouped data frames passed emoji_summary(), emoji_frequency() top_n_emojis() now warn grouping ignored (per-group results land 1.0). Lifecycle badge downgraded stable maturing. Vignette sample renamed ata_tweets.rda (CSV misnamed .rda) ata_tweets.csv downsampled 10k 2k rows. Vignette language updated less Twitter-specific. Crosswalk datasets rebuilt key column normalised joins.

title: tidyEmoji 0.2.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-06-17 tidyEmoji now positioned general toolkit emoji text column (social-media posts, reviews, chat logs, survey responses, …), just tweets.

title: tidyEmoji 0.2.0
text: emoji_sentiment() scores emoji row using bundled emoji_sentiment_lexicon (Emoji Sentiment Ranking Kralj Novak et al., 2015), returning mean sentiment [-1, 1]. emoji_frequency() returns count every emoji text column, name, shortcode category. top_n_emojis() now thin wrapper . emoji_tokens() expands data one row per emoji occurrence name, category sentiment score — tidy, “one-token-per-row” shape. emoji_filter() clearer, text-agnostic name emoji_tweets() (kept synonym). New bundled dataset emoji_sentiment_lexicon.

title: tidyEmoji 0.2.0
text: Grapheme-aware detection. Extraction now keeps skin-tone modifiers zero-width-joiner sequences intact. Previously family emoji (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦) miscounted four separate people skin-tone thumbs-split two “emoji”; now counted one. Much faster. Detection counting longer build multi-thousand-way regular expression every call scan text per known emoji; top_n_emojis() particular dramatically faster large inputs. top_n_emojis() longer emits many--many join warning, reports emoji’s canonical shortcode (e.g. mask) default. verbs now return tibbles consistently (emoji_tweets() previously returned plain data frame), emoji_extract_unnest() longer prints grouping message. Bundled emoji data refreshed current Unicode emoji list (via data-raw/).

title: tidyEmoji 0.2.0
text: Arguments renamed tweet_tbl -> data tweet_text -> text. Code passed positionally (e.g. df %>% emoji_summary(text_col)) unaffected; update calls named old arguments. top_n_emojis(duplicated_unicode = "yes"/"") deprecated favour logical duplicated = TRUE/FALSE. old argument still works warning.
